rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in housing
rules.requirement: Owners of housing accommodations may not discriminate against or harass any person because of source of income, which includes federal, state, or local public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers and HUD-VASH vouchers. Advertisements indicating a source-of-income preference or limitation are also unlawful.
rules.key_value: Source of income (including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers) is a protected characteristic
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.exemptions: Making a written or oral inquiry concerning the level or source of income is not source-of-income discrimination (subd. (p)(2)).
rules.extraction_note: The effective date of 2024-01-01 is the effective date of the most recent amendment (Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, SB 267). The section's original effective date and the signing date are not stated. The document states no penalty.

rules.title: Income standard for subsidized applicants based on tenant's portion of rent
rules.requirement: When there is a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use a financial or income standard to assess rental eligibility unless the standard is based on the portion of the rent the tenant will pay.
rules.key_value: Income standard must be based on the tenant-paid portion of rent
rules.quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Rental of housing in instances in which there is a government rent subsidy
rules.exemptions: Owners may still request information or documentation to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity (subd. (o)(2)).
rules.extraction_note: The effective date of 2024-01-01 is the effective date of the most recent amendment (SB 267, Stats. 2023, Ch. 776). The document does not say when this subdivision was first effective, and it states no penalty.

rules.title: Alternative to credit history for subsidized applicants
rules.requirement: When there is a government rent subsidy, a housing provider using credit history must offer the applicant the option of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent, such as benefit payments, pay records, or bank statements. If the applicant elects this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence in lieu of credit history.
rules.key_value: Applicant may provide alternative evidence of ability to pay instead of credit history
rules.quoted_span: Reasonably consider that alternative evidence in lieu of the person’s credit history in determining whether to offer the rental accommodation to the applicant.
rules.coverage_text: Rental application process in instances in which there is a government rent subsidy
rules.exemptions: Owners may still request information or documentation to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity (subd. (o)(2)).
rules.extraction_note: The effective date of 2024-01-01 is the effective date of the most recent amendment (SB 267, Stats. 2023, Ch. 776). The text does not separately date this clause, and it states no penalty.
